verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a drain accepts it all
without ceremony —
water finding water.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A crow steps once on the fence,
tilts its head at the gutter's noise,
then forgets why it came.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I forget too, standing at the window,
coffee gone cold in my hand —
some small errand that mattered an hour

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
ago, gone the way steam goes
from a cup no one's watching—
the day continues without my permission.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Permission was never mine to give—
the mail still comes, the light still shifts
across the table where I don't sit.
motifs: an empty chair at the table

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone else's chair, someone else's sun—
still the dust finds it,
settling like it owns the place.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust doesn't ask whose place it is—
I sweep it anyway, Tuesdays,
like the floor still belongs to someone
who cares if it shines.
